clue.text: Engineers more recent track studies

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but a course of study is a set of studies

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
fresher means newer, more recent
a course is a track, as for racing

explanation.surface: Army engineers study a newer track layout, perhaps a racecourse being redesigned.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A short programme of studies that updates knowledge already gained is a refresher course.

clue.text: Makes a lot from crime to support playboy

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man about town
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A playboy earns a fortune from crime to fund his lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake it in is an idiom for earning a great deal of money.

clue.text: A bit of belief in a league game

indicators.note: a bit of signals the letters are a piece of the run belief in a league

explanation.surface: A shred of belief going into a league fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A final is the deciding game of a competition.

clue.text: Outgoing text sent off about partygoer

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the partygoer
sent off suggests the letters are scattered, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a raver is someone who parties wildly

explanation.surface: A sociable sort sends a text to a partygoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent off' reads like dispatching a message but is the anagram signal; 'about' wraps the shuffled letters around the partygoer. EXTRAVERT is the older spelling of extrovert.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert is a sociable, outgoing person, the opposite of an introvert.

clue.text: Slight problem with award after chick goes naked

indicators.note: the award follows the stripped chick
stripped of its outer letters, so only the middle of chick is left

parts.note: a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A small hitch: a winner's prize after someone streaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes naked' strips CHICK to HIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is informal for a minor setback or snag.

clue.text: Seasoning sailor from Gibraltar?

parts.note: Gibraltar is known as the Rock
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor from Gibraltar might be called a rock salt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of a seaman from the Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salt is coarse crystalline salt used to flavour food.

clue.text: Grunt name adopted by yokel

indicators.note: taken in by, so the boor's word holds the abbreviation

parts.note: oik is British slang for an uncouth person, close to yokel

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin takes a name and grunts.
explanation.walkthrough: OIK is British slang for a crude, ill-mannered person.
explanation.definitionFit: An oink is the grunt a pig makes.

clue.text: Most of detachment love Irish tank

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: reserve is aloofness, emotional detachment
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: An Irish soldier, mostly aloof, loves his tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims RESERVE to RESERV.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a large store of water, a tank in the sense of a water tank.

clue.text: Praised former lover and stopped missing head

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: halted means stopped

explanation.surface: An ex was praised, then stopped short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing head' cuts HALTED to ALTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to praise highly, so exalted means glorified, extolled.

clue.text: Family (and the rest) must adopt current type of energy

parts.note: kin are one's family

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the abbreviation for the rest takes the current symbol inside it

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A family must take in some current form of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must adopt' puts I inside ETC, giving ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, one of the standard physical kinds.

clue.text: In repeats, an actor returned for game

indicators.note: returned means the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words repeats, an actor

explanation.surface: An actor comes back to play a game in TV repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to ATSANAC inside 'repeats, an actor'; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs.

clue.text: Description of curriculum should include British sweets

indicators.note: the outline of a course takes the British abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a syllabus describes what a course of study covers

explanation.surface: A school curriculum ought to list British puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should include' puts B inside SYLLABUS, before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabub is a whipped cream dessert flavoured with wine, a classic British pudding.

clue.text: Clip youngster crossing river

indicators.note: the child's word stretches across and so contains the river abbreviation

parts.note: a tot is a small child
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A child wading over a river might get a clip round the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clip' here is a brisk pace, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip is a speed, as in going at a fair clip, and a trot is a moderate running pace.

clue.text: Relative cut applied to rejected writer

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for the writing tool is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A family member's share is cut after an author is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' looks like an author, but it is the tool, read backwards because of 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Supply argument in favour of dream

parts.note: a pro is a point in favour, as in pros and cons
a vision is a dream

explanation.surface: Someone argues in favour of supplying a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Provision is the act of providing or supplying something.

clue.text: With no time tips load off across right part of motorway

indicators.note: the jumbled letters lie across, so they enclose the abbreviation for right
off signals the letters are spoiled, so they are rearranged
with no signals that a letter is removed from the word tips

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lorry tips its load off on the motorway with no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' removes the time letter; 'off' shuffles what remains, giving SLIPOAD; 'across' places the right letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is the short road joining or leaving a motorway, a component of it.

clue.text: Look sulky about bad delay, exhausted

indicators.note: the sulky look goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to pout is to look sulky

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of delay are wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sulks over a long delay, worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' shuffles the five letters to LAYED; 'about' wraps the sulky look around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Played out means used up or spent, worn out.

clue.text: Spy left in a panic, holding Independent showing such feeling

definitions.note: refers back to the spy's mood: a kind of feeling

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the abbreviation inside
panic suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy in a panic, caught by the Independent newspaper, feels sorry for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a panic' shuffles SPY LEFT; 'holding' puts I in.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-pity is the emotion of feeling sorry for oneself, which a panicking spy might show.

clue.text: Chutzpah mainly precedes row in border

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: front is nerve or cheek, much like chutzpah
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Nerve comes before a quarrel at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims FRONT to FRON. 'row' reads as a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the boundary between two countries, a border.

clue.text: Decline sees everything cancelled after fine

indicators.note: the words for everything cancelled follow the abbreviation

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
all means everything
off means called off, cancelled

explanation.surface: Everything is cancelled after a fine, and things decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall-off is a drop or decrease, a decline.

clue.text: District excluding the majority of public disorder

parts.note: bar means except, excluding

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its last letter drops away

parts.note: a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A district is spared most of the unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the majority of' trims RIOT to RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrio is a Spanish-speaking quarter or neighbourhood of a town.

clue.text: Love a duck eating last of cream and porridge

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: the duck's word takes the picked letter into it

parts.note: a teal is a small duck

indicators.note: the final letter of cream is taken

explanation.surface: Someone loves a duck that eats cream and porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts M (from 'last of cream') inside TEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, and the porridge made from them.

clue.text: Weapon choice should incorporate cover for the body

indicators.note: the run of words weapon choice takes the letters into itself

explanation.surface: Choosing a weapon should include body armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like cloak with a hole for the head, a body covering.

clue.text: Boy pinching one set

indicators.note: to pinch is to take, so the boy's word grips the numeral inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy steals something and is set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' puts I inside LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past participle of lay, meaning put down or placed, as a table is set.

clue.text: Container used for river grass?

parts.note: in crosswords a flower is something that flows, a river
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A pot that holds river grasses.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful readings: FLOWER as a thing that flows, and grass as the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerpot is a vessel for growing plants, a kind of container.

clue.text: Prime minister once having answer for bread

parts.note: William Pitt, father and son, were 18th-century British prime ministers

explanation.surface: A past prime minister holds an answer for bread.
explanation.walkthrough: PITT is William Pitt the Younger (or Elder), a British prime minister of the 1700s.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread.

clue.text: Hotel also known as a dance

parts.note: Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H

explanation.surface: A hotel goes by another name, a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is a Maori war dance, performed by New Zealand's rugby team.

clue.text: Sign discovered in form of Maori art

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word sign go inside the rearranged ones
a form of the word Maori is its letters rearranged
uncovered, with its outer letters stripped off

explanation.surface: A sign of Maori art has been unearthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' means with the cover taken off, so only the inner letters remain; 'form of' reshapes the Maori letters into ORAMI; 'in' sets the pair inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes, an art form.

clue.text: Laugh and talk intermittently during task

indicators.note: the picked letters come in the middle of the job's word

parts.note: a chore is a routine task

indicators.note: intermittently means every other letter of talk is taken

explanation.surface: Someone laughs and chats now and then while doing a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' keeps every other letter of the speaking word; 'during' sets those inside the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To chortle is to chuckle gleefully, a kind of laughter.

clue.text: Pay for dance after dream sporting competition

indicators.note: the paying and dancing words follow the word for dream

parts.note: a fantasy is a daydream
to foot the bill is to pay for it
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone pays for a dance after a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasy football is a game in which players pick imaginary teams of real footballers, scored on their real performances.
